page: Amazon Web Services c9g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton9 processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The underlying hardware utilizes the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 microarchitecture, equipped with 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.2xlarge demonstrates strong single-threaded performance in specific data processing tasks. It achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.44 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.31 GB/sec. Memory performance is also a highlight, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top tier, supported by a cached read-only small block memory bandwidth of 1085.97 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded operations and raw CPU benchmarks, such as the stress-ng multi-core test and PassMark CPU score, fall within the average tier. Cryptographic performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25% due to the lack of certain advanced vector and matrix extensions.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c9g.2xlarge offers high compute density and memory bandwidth relative to its resource footprint, making it an efficient choice for ARM-native workloads. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent performance without hyperthreading overhead. This instance is well-suited for single-threaded data compression, lightweight web serving, Redis key-value stores, and small-scale language model text generation. It is less optimal for heavy cryptographic processing or workloads requiring high-capacity local storage.
